newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas soft across curve as producer offers fal.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas soft across curve as producer offers fal.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices were softer across the forward curve on Wednesday, traders and brokers said.
Deals were evenly spread for all periods from the day ahead through to the summer of 1998 and possibly beyond.
One trader said prices could fall further over the summer, pointed out that several producers are now offering gas aggressively.
The news of the sale of balancing margins gas by Transco as well as the knowledge that J-Block gas will be on the market earlier than expected were all said to be adding to the pressure on prices.
Another dealer dismissed this view, saying that the current weakness had nothing to do with fundamentals. "It's just that somebody wants it down," he said.
On the day ahead market prices were stable at the NBP, with trade seen art 11.20 pence a therm.
There was at least one day ahead deal done at St Fergus, on a private and confidential basis with the exact price unknown.

But it was confirmed that the price achieved at St Fergus put that terminal at a premium to the NBP when it is normally at a discount to the NBP. But a dealer said this premium was only evident on the short term market, with St Fergus reverting to a discount of around 0.20 pence a therm for all but the very prompt market.
Q3, Q4 and Q1 were all actively traded, all at lower numbers than on Tuesday, and summer 1998 also saw a good volume of trade.
There were also said to have been some year deals.

It was widely reported, though not confirmed, that the 1997 gas year was done at 12.80 pence. This was thought to be an outright price. It was also reported that 12.75 pence had been done for the same period, although this was also unconfirmed, and at least two players said it was believed to be a spread against another year, making the outright price less important than the differential.

Transco reported that the SAP for Tuesday 3 June was 0.3996 p/kWh (11.71 pence a therm), the same level as for the 7-day rolling average. The 30-day average stood at 0.3991 p/kWh, or around 11.70 pence a therm.

The IPE was weaker on Wednesday in line with the OTC market, but deals were only done in 2 months, July, which traded at 10.30 pence and settled at 10.18 pence, and September, which traded and settled at 10.20 pence. A total of 25 lots were done.
